newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian bank poll shows optimistic 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian bank poll shows optimistic 1997 outlook.

text.p: Prospects for Brazil's economy look bright for 1997, according to a survey of 10 national banks published Sunday in Brazilian newspapers.
Of the 10 banks polled, only one, Unibanco, expected inflation of 10 percent, with the other nine forecasting inflation of between seven and 9.5 percent, said O Globo newspaper.
Forecasts for 1996 inflation are between 10 and 12 percent and a fall to below 10 percent would be the first time Brazil had single digit inflation since 1957, O Estado de Sao Paulo said.

Interest rates are generally expected to fall in the second half of the year, averaging around 21 percent in the first six months, before dropping to 19 percent in the July to December period, O Globo said.
Nine of the banks anticipate a reduction in the public deficit while the tenth, FonteCindam, forecasts the deficit to remain steady.
GDP is seen growing at an average of four percent, with Cindam and Unibanco the most reserved with estimates of 3.5 percent and Linear the most bullish at five percent.

Estimates of the trade deficit averaged $3.8 billion, ranging between $1.5 billion from Bic Banco to $5.5 billion from Cindam, while reserves were expected to fall slightly, with the average forecast at $55.6 billion.
The 10 banks polled were ABC-Roma, BCN, Bic Banco, Citibank, Cindam, ING Bank, Linear, Opportunity, Unibanco and Matrix.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
